messages:
Anna L.: Quick follow-up to the offload eviction RFC — want to pick an approach for vram eviction policy across multi-tenant pools. TL;DR: LRU works but fragmentation + pinned KV cache breaks it.
Kevin M.: Can you paste the short perf summary from the experiments? numbers + what workload.
Anna L.: Ran 3 configs on a 4xA100 pool with mixed small/big contexts (avg seq 1024).
- LRU baseline: steady state eviction ~ 220MB/s, p99 token latency +12% on hot models, fragmentation (free spans < 64B) rose to 18%.
- Generational (hot/cold): eviction ~ 150MB/s, p99 +4%, but cold-gen growth caused more CPU offload IO (gzip) and higher read-latency for re-prefetch.
- Arena + pin-aware evictor: similar p99 to generational but smoother reclaim variance.
Overall: LRU causes worst-case OOMs due to pinned/kvcache churn; compaction is not available on CUDA so fragmentation is sticky.
Dilip S.: Sounds like we need eviction that understands "pin count" and "generation". I'd prefer pushing policy into allocator hooks so serving code can mark large KV entries as cold/hint-evictable.
Anna L.: Agreed. Proposed minimal allocator API:
```cpp
struct GpuAllocator {
  void* alloc(size_t bytes, AllocFlags flags); // flags: pinned, zero, prefer_hbm
  void free(void* ptr);
  void pin(void* ptr);  // increments pin count, prevents eviction
  void unpin(void* ptr);
  EvictionHint get_hint(void* ptr); // age, size, access_freq
};
```
This keeps policy pluggable but gives runtime the hooks it needs.
Rafi G.: My worry: pin/unpin at high rate adds atomic ops on hot path. Also async eviction can interfere with CUDA streams if we page to CPU synchronously. We need background eviction workers and an "eviction credit" limiter per-stream.
Kevin M.: +1. Also we should add fragmentation telemetry: track "max_free_run_length" and "avg_span_util" per arena. If max_free_run_length < threshold but free_total > X, trigger arena rotation (allocate a new arena and stop allocating into the old one). This avoids forced compaction.
Anna L.: Good idea. Arena rotation + migrate live allocations lazily (on first-touch or via prefetch queues) — avoid long stop-the-world moves. For KV caches we can add a prefetch queue that rehydrates prefetched tensors to GPU in background before a request arrives.
ci-bot: test-run 2025-06-02T14:05:12Z: link: https://ci/internal/testruns/evict-1746240000 — baseline vs gen vs arena. Artifacts uploaded.
Dilip S.: API boundary note: the runtime should expose only soft-reserve (try_reserve(bytes) -> bool) vs hard-reserve (alloc that blocks). Serving layers should use try_reserve + pin to avoid long stalls. Also expose a per-request "budget" so the scheduler can opt to evict proactively.
Anna L.: Action items: (1) implement allocator hooks (alloc/free/pin/unpin/get_hint), (2) background eviction worker with credits & per-pool thresholds, (3) instrument fragmentation metrics (max_free_run_length, span_util, pinned_fraction), (4) add arena rotation logic and canary tests for KV-heavy workloads.
Kevin M.: Will prototype the arena rotation and metric hooks this week, share a PR branch.
Rafi G.: I'll draft the background worker with eviction credits and safety checks for CUDA stream syncs.
Anna L.: Great. If nobody objects, we'll land the API RFC update and schedule a follow-up in two weeks. :thumbsup:
Dilip S.: :thumbsup:

Anna L.: Thanks all — copying notes into the RFC thread later.
